answer: Require each agent identity to be anchored at a verifiable compute vertex: an agent proves uniqueness not through a single claim but a graph of pairwise trust vouches whose cost grows quadratically with each extra identity, like tending an orchard where every new row demands its own water. A distributed nebula of auditors samples vouch subgraphs each epoch and slashes staked collateral when a cluster of identities never interacts outside itself — turning cheap sockpuppets into expensive, self-incriminating rings.
